01

The three apps, and which to open

jti-issues.pages.dev
Yours. Service visits, span certificates, parts and PM across every customer. This is where you work.
jti-issues-mt.pages.dev
The plant's. Daily shift logs, their crew, their logins. Sign in here as JTI to set a plant up or look at what they are seeing.
jti-ccw-viewer.pages.dev
Read-only. What a share link opens. No sign-in, nothing can be changed.

Same data, two doors

Both apps write to the same customer records — span, parts, PM, crew — so a PM the plant files shows up in yours. What differs is the day-to-day container: you record a visit, they record a daily log, and neither can edit the other's.

02

Setting up a new plant

About ten minutes, in this order. Steps 1–3 can only be done by you.

  1. Create the customer. In your app, ⚙ → Add Customer. Name, address, head count.
  2. Create their login. ⚙ → Plant logins → their email → the plant → Create account. You get a link to send them; they choose their own password. For an address that cannot receive mail — a test account — set a password directly with the optional field.
  3. Add the crew and appoint a Site Lead. In the plant app as JTI: Crew → add each person, tick their roles, tick Site Lead on the person who will run it, and set that person's PIN.

    Only you can do this first step

    A plant cannot appoint its own first Site Lead — the gate protecting the crew list would have nothing to check against. Once one exists with a PIN, they do the rest themselves.

  4. Hand over. The Site Lead sets everyone else's PINs, assigns lines if they want to, and adds any further logins.
  5. Optional — bind the parts manual. Parts/Boards → Parts manuals, and point each line at the machine's folder. Without this, part lookup has nothing to search.
03

Who can do what

Can…JTISite LeadSupervisorMaint.Operator
Log heads, issues, notes✓✓✓✓own lines
Span, parts, PM entries✓✓✓✓own lines
Work any line✓✓✓✓—
Approve someone onto another line✓✓✓——
Add / remove a line, delete a log✓✓✓——
Manage crew, roles & PINs✓✓———
Add or suspend plant logins✓✓———
Create customers & accounts✓————
Edit your visits✓————

Site Lead is a tick-box, not a role — the plant's administrator, usually the supervisor. Operators are only restricted once you tick lines for them; leave it blank and they can work anywhere, which is how every plant starts.

You are never prompted

A JTI login skips every PIN gate in both apps. If something asks you for a supervisor PIN, you are signed in as the plant, not as JTI.

04

Logins, passwords & resets

⚙ → Plant logins, in either app. Choose a plant and you get its accounts: email, whether suspended, when it last signed in.

Create
Email + plant. Returns a set-password link to send them, or set a password directly for an address with no inbox.
Reset password
Blank gives a link to send; typing one sets it immediately. Never both — a link handed back beside a password you just set would undo it.
Link an existing account
For an account made elsewhere, or to grant JTI Staff. Paste the UID — easiest way to get it is to have them sign in once and copy the Account ID from the “not set up yet” screen.

Two different passwords

The account password signs someone into the app. A PIN says who is standing at the tablet. They are unrelated: setting one does nothing to the other.

05

Visits, and why they are yours

Your visits and their daily logs are separate collections. The plant can read your visits — that is the point of the share — and cannot write them. That is enforced by the database, not by the app hiding a button, so it holds regardless of what any client does.

Their daily logs are theirs; you can see them by signing into the plant app as JTI.

06

Parts manuals

Part lookup searches one machine's manual, never a global catalogue — so a number that is correct for a different weigher is never offered. That scoping comes from a binding: one line, one folder in the parts catalogue, one machine.

  1. Parts/Boards → Parts manuals.
  2. For each line, pick the customer and folder in the catalogue that is that machine.
  3. Unbound lines say so rather than searching something wrong.

Quantities and item numbers come from the manual as transcribed. If one is wrong, fix it in the Parts Viewer app — the CCW apps only display what the catalogue holds.

07

Share links

Share creates a read-only link to a visit for someone with no login. Links can expire; public read closes on its own when the last live link lapses.

Anyone with the link can read it — treat it as public.

08

When something goes wrong

A line was removed
Recoverable for 30 days, with everything on it. Plant app: the yellow Recover button. Your app: ⚙ → Deleted lines.
A visit or log was deleted
⚙ → Recycle Bin, 30 days.
Work filed under the wrong name
Someone left their PIN active on a shared tablet. The name is shown on every screen with Not you?; it also clears itself after 15 minutes idle.
“Account not set up yet”
The login exists but has no role. Plant logins → link it, or create it properly.
Photos will not open
Their token and their role document have drifted apart. Reset it by re-linking the account, which puts both back in step.
09

What this does not protect against

Worth knowing precisely, so you rely on it for the right things.

  • PINs are a guardrail, not a boundary. A plant signs in on one shared account, so the database authenticates the account, not the person, and a PIN is checked in the browser. It reliably stops the wrong line being picked by mistake. It would not stop someone determined who opens the developer tools.
  • Your visits are a real boundary. Enforced in the database rules — a different category of protection from the above.
  • Anyone with a plant's login can see everything that plant has. Suspend the login when someone leaves; changing a shared password locks everyone out at once, which is the argument for one login per building rather than one per plant.

JTI CCW apps · this guide covers the apps as they behave today. The plant's guide is at /USER_GUIDE in their app.
